prompt: Write a command that uses Invoke-RestMethod to make a GET request to 'https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts/1'.
hints: GET is the default method, so you don't need -Method.

validation.hintOnFail: Specify the URL with the -Uri parameter.

explanation: Invoke-RestMethod sends a GET request by default. It automatically parses the JSON response into a PowerShell object with properties like title, body, and userId.

prompt: Create a hashtable called $headers with an 'Authorization' key set to 'Bearer abc123', then pass it to Invoke-RestMethod using the -Headers parameter for a GET request to 'https://api.example.com/data'.
hints: The complete command has two lines: the hashtable definition and the Invoke-RestMethod call.

validation.hintOnFail: Store the headers in a variable called $headers.
Set the Authorization key to 'Bearer abc123'.
Use Invoke-RestMethod to make the request.

explanation: The headers hashtable passes HTTP headers to the API. The Authorization header with a Bearer token is the most common way to authenticate with REST APIs.

prompt: Write a command that sends a POST request to 'https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts' with a JSON body containing a 'title' of 'Test' and a 'body' of 'Content'. Use ConvertTo-Json and set the content type.
hints: Create a hashtable with title and body keys, then pipe it to ConvertTo-Json.
Store the JSON in a variable first, then pass it with -Body.

validation.hintOnFail: Use Invoke-RestMethod to send the request.
Use Post as the HTTP method.
Convert the body hashtable to JSON with ConvertTo-Json.
Pass the JSON string using the -Body parameter.

explanation: The hashtable is converted to a JSON string with ConvertTo-Json. Invoke-RestMethod sends it as a POST request. The -ContentType header tells the API the body is JSON.

prompt: Write a command that calls Invoke-RestMethod inside a try/catch block, using -ErrorAction Stop so exceptions are caught. In the catch block, write the error message using Write-Warning.
hints: Wrap the Invoke-RestMethod call in try { ... }.
Add -ErrorAction Stop so non-terminating errors become catchable.

validation.hintOnFail: Add a catch block to handle errors.
Call Invoke-RestMethod inside the try block.
Use -ErrorAction Stop to make errors catchable.
Use Write-Warning in the catch block to display the error.

explanation: The -ErrorAction Stop parameter converts non-terminating errors into terminating exceptions that the catch block can handle. Write-Warning outputs the error message as a warning.
